newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq welcomes French withdrawal from air missions.
newsitem.headline: Iraq welcomes French withdrawal from air missions.

text.p: Iraq on Saturday welcomed France's decision to withdraw from a U.S.-led air reconnaissance operation in its Kurdish north, the official Iraqi News Agency INA reported.

"Iraq welcomes the French decision and regards it as a positive and important step which expresses France's understanding that the no-fly zone in northern Iraq imposed by the Americans and British is illegal," said an Iraqi Foreign Ministry statement, carried by INA.
France said on Friday it was withdrawing at the end of the year from the five-year-old allied operation aimed at protecting Iraqi Kurds from possible attacks by Baghdad.
The French Foreign Ministry said the main goal of the operation had until now been to assure the safety of humanitarian flights by private aid groups into northern Iraq.
This would no longer be necessary because a United Nations food-for-oil deal required that 30 percent of all aid destined for Iraq should be earmarked for Kurdish areas, France said.
The move did not afffect French participation in a similar air watch over southern Iraq with U.S. and British aircraft, the French Foreign Ministry said.

The Iraqi Foreign Ministry statement urged France to withdraw from the no-fly zone in southern Iraq. "At the time that Iraq highly appreciates the French decision, it hopes that France would do the same thing regarding the no-fly zone in southern Iraq," the ministry said.

Turkey on Wednesday allowed the United States and Britain to continue using its airbases to fly sorties in northern Iraq. Baghdad condemned Ankara for the move and an Iraqi official newspaper said: "The Turkish decision...smells of a conspiracy against Iraq."
France has about half a dozen planes in the mission, which is centred on Incerlik Air Base in Turkey.

It temporarily halted its flights in September after the United States fired 44 cruise missiles against targets in the south of Iraq to retaliate against President Saddam Hussein for moving ground troops into a Kurdish enclave north of the 36th parallel.
